experiment: inverse adjuster — where the dial recovers the best per-round outcomes
verdict: WORKING BACKWARDS: the adjuster setting that recovers the most best-value skill players is a VALUE ANCHOR AT ~BEST-AVAILABLE — the market already surfaces the top-3-VORP player in its top 3 available at 19/41 picks (46%), no special dial needed. A value-over-market TILT recovers 4 more of the 26 value-signal picks (2024-25). 8 are UNREACHABLE by either signal — no setting gets them without fitting noise. This is a THIRD independent confirmation of the measured mask+value rule (after the participation test and the strategy tournament): the knobs that earn are value + best-available, and tuning the others chases the unreachable. BIG CAVEAT: 25/41 of the 'best value available' were ELITE QBs the market faded — but single-QB VORP OVERSTATES value in our 1-QB league (you start one; a top-10 QB is streamable), which is exactly why the dollar-graded tournament did NOT reward QB-early. So VORP flags QB as unclaimed, the dollars say the room is right to fade it — do NOT tune the adjuster to chase QB. The real recoverable value is the non-QB skill our value signal caught (e.g. Brock Bowers); the real leak in Cory's own drafts is REACHING past best-available onto busts (Quentin Johnston -163, Joe Burrow '25 -160 VORP).
caveat: Two reconstructable signals (market always, value 2024-25). REALIZED defines the targets only. 'Recovered' = a top-3-realized available player ranks in a signal's top-3 available. 2023 is market-only (no prior for walk_forward). Value signal is our walk_forward model, which is weaker than the consensus the board uses, so value-recovery here is a FLOOR — the real board's consensus would recover more. Installs nothing; maps what the adjusters can and cannot reach.
